sensitivity_on_inter_species_reassortant.definition: PRIMARY. correct = gate1 named the exact segment that was exchanged.
sensitivity_on_inter_species_reassortant.unresolvable_note: gate1 named the right segment but returned 'undetectable_by_design' because the two candidate parent species are too close to tell apart. The exchange was found; the parents were not. Note that this is also the VERDICT the user reads.

known_blind_spot_intra_species.note: These are REAL published reassortants that gate1 cannot see, because both parents assign to the same reference species. This is a measured limitation, not a passing test. gate4 phylogenetics is the layer that would catch them.

results.paper: Rizvanov, Khaiboullina & St Jeor (2004) Virology 327:225-232, doi:10.1016/j.virol.2004.07.012
results.reported: Reassortants generated in vitro between Sin Nombre virus and Andes virus. Viable progeny carried the SNV S and L segments with the ANDV M segment; no S- or L-exchanged reassortant was recovered.

results.paper: Rizvanov, Khaiboullina & St Jeor (2004) Virology 327:225-232
results.reported: Reciprocal orientation of the same SNV x ANDV cross. Included as a directionality control: the detector must not be sensitive to which parent is called the backbone.

results.paper: Handke, Oelschlegel, Franke, Wiedemann, Kruger & Rang (2010) J Gen Virol 91:2351-2359, doi:10.1099/vir.0.021139-0
results.reported: Genetic reassortants generated between Puumala virus and Prospect Hill virus. Only M-segment exchange yielded viable reassortants.

results.paper: Rodriguez, Owens, Peters & Nichol (1998) Virology 242:99-106, doi:10.1006/viro.1997.8990
results.reported: Genetic reassortment among Sin Nombre viruses causing hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. Coinfection of SNV strains NM R11 and Convict Creek 107 (CC107) at MOI 1 yielded 25 reassortants; Table 7 records 12 M-exchanged and 12 S-exchanged progeny.

results.paper: Rodriguez et al. (1998) Virology 242:99-106, Table 7
results.reported: The S-exchanged arm of the same experiment (12 of 25 reassortants). Rodriguez's central result is that S exchange is as frequent as M exchange between close parents.
Review: intra- and inter-lineage reassortment repeatedly reported for Dobrava-Belgrade virus among its Apodemus-associated genotypes.

results.paper: Park, Kim, Kim, Kim & Song (2025) Sci Rep, doi:10.1038/s41598-025-11003-z
results.reported: Longitudinal genomic surveillance of Orthohantavirus hantanense in the Republic of Korea reports reassortant candidates with heterogeneous L segments, i.e. S/L and M/L incongruence within the species.

results.paper: Klempa (2018) Virus Genes 54:638-646
results.reported: Review: intra-lineage reassortment repeatedly reported for Puumala virus among European lineages.
